description: This is update number 10 in the US Department of Energy's series of situation reports on Hurricane Ida, issued at 11:00 AM EDT on 7 September 2021 for public distribution, nine days after the Category 4 storm made landfall near Port Fourchon, Louisiana. The electricity section reports about 465,000 customer outages remaining in Louisiana, Entergy's work to restore the transmission system serving New Orleans, estimated restoration dates by parish (September 8 for Orleans, up to September 29 for the hardest-hit parishes) and more than 27,000 mutual-assistance workers from 41 states. The oil and natural gas section reports five Louisiana refineries shut, about 1.0 million barrels per day or 6% of US refining capacity, with 84% of federal Gulf of Mexico oil and 81% of gas production shut in, and discusses fuel supply chain and retail station impacts. Access: free PDF on the energy.gov site; no licence is stated. Coverage is Louisiana and neighbouring Gulf states for one date. Caveats: it is a snapshot narrative report, not a data series, and figures changed in later updates. It suits resilience and emergency response studies of storm impacts on power and fuel systems, and relates to the EAGLE-I county outage record catalogued here.
